   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  CITY CLERK’S OFFICE

  MEMORANDUM

 TO:  City Council Newspaper/Advertising Ad Hoc Committee Liaisons

 FROM:  Huma Ahmed, City Clerk
  Michelle Ramos-Vergara, Deputy City Clerk
  Anthony Rodstein, Purchasing Services Manager

 DATE:  May 9, 2025

 SUBJECT:  Discussion Regarding the Annual Draft FY 2025-26 Advertising and
  Notices Bid

 ATTACHMENTS:  None

INTRODUCTION

The City of Beverly Hills is required to conduct an annual bid for legal advertisements with
adjudicated newspapers located in Beverly Hills. The annual bid has historically included display
advertising. The bid does not require the City to award the contract to the lowest bidder.

With no case law on this subject, the Public Contracts Code provides City Council the discretion
to award contracts to qualified newspapers based on price and public value. In the past few years,
the City Council has based their decision on the Beverly Hills circulation data submitted by each
newspaper within their audit report.

DISCUSSION

For this current fiscal year, at the May 7, 2024 City Council Study Session, staff presented City
Council with an overview of the FY 2024-25 bids submitted by three locally adjudicated
newspapers: the BH Courier Acquisition, LLC (Courier), Beverly Hills Weekly (Weekly), and
Beverly Press/Park La Brea News (Press). After much discussion, the City Council agreed to
award the Bid to the Courier and to contract with the Weekly and the Press at rates based on a
replication of the previous year’s award methodology: using the Courier’s circulation rates within
Beverly Hills as the primary metric, and scaling down their line item bid prices to determine ad
rate pricing and contract amounts for the other two publications.

At the same meeting, the Beverly Hills Press expressed disappointment at the methodology used,
stating that the awarded rates were insufficient to cover their costs especially costs related to their
staffing and to the size and scope of their publication. At the time, their Certified Verification
Circulation Audit reported that their Beverly Hills circulation was much lower than those of the
Courier and Weekly. However, despite lower delivery circulation than the other two publications,
the Press pointed out that in addition, they also share content on their website which had 750,000
users. The Press requested fairness in the City Council's advertising budget award due to their
reach adjacent to and outside of Beverly Hills.
 For this new fiscal year, the City Council suggested for the FY 2025-26 Bid that the Ad Hoc Liaison
consider outside Beverly Hills circulation for display ads and to review digital and social media
metrics and how they may impact each newspapers’ outreach.

Per previous City Council direction, the following online metrics were required to be included in
the audit for the newspapers’ 12-month audit period (October 2023 to September 2024) for the
FY 25-26 Bid (this year’s bid).
 Audited Average Website Reporting
 Audited Online/Digital Edition Reporting
 Text Media (Distribution Reporting)
 Email Media (Distribution Reporting)

Based on this direction, staff proposes the following award methodologies for the FY 25-26 Bid:

Option 1: Circulation within Beverly Hills
This option suggests no change to the practice and is a replication of last year’s award
methodology, using circulation rates within Beverly Hills of the winning bidder as the primary
metric, and scaling down the winning line item bid prices of the winning publication to determine
ad rate pricing and contract amounts for the other publications.

Option 2: Circulation within Beverly Hills and outside the City (90/10 circulation formula)
This option blends circulation within Beverly Hills and outside of Beverly Hills using a weighted
formula to reflect the value of display ads being presented to neighboring communities. Under
this option, each publication’s circulation within Beverly Hills is weighted at 90% and circulation
outside of Beverly Hills is weighted at 10%. Each publication’s circulation at the aforementioned
weights is calculated to determine award points, a winning bidder is designated, and each other
publication has their bid rates scaled down by a proportion of award points relative to the winning
bidder.

Option 3: Circulation within Beverly Hills, outside the City, and online metrics (90/5/5 circulation
formula)
This option builds upon Option 2 and adds in a consideration of a newspaper’s online readership,
reflecting the value of online outreach. As each newspaper’s online metrics were required to be
included in the most recent CVC audit, staff will have this metric to run comparisons. Staff
proposes an award formula as follows:
   90% circulation within Beverly Hills
   5% circulation outside the City
   5% online readership

Option 4: Acceptance and award of all bids
This option entails the City designating a winning bid for legal and display advertising, and making
awards to other publications as in the best interests of the City. Under this option, the City would
accept and award the ad bid rates from the other publications received through the bid process,
with no adjustment based on the circulation formula.

Please note that if the City Council agrees to raise the rates, use of any other calculation than
what has been traditionally used, may affect the number of ads placed and result in increased
costs to the City.

 FISCAL IMPACT

The legal and display advertising budgets are placeholders and are only paid to each
newspaper based on the services rendered. Funds are not guaranteed to any single
publisher. The City may opt to increase or decrease the placement of ads as needed.

The budget for legal advertisements is managed through the City Clerk’s Office, while the budget
for non-legal/display advertising is managed through the Communications Office.
The City Clerk Office’s FY 2025-26 budget for legal advertising and notices is $112,482. The
Citywide FY 2025-26 budget for display advertising is $543,558.20. The total advertising budget
is $656,040.20. There are no set fixed amounts designated for each newspaper -
advertisements are placed as needed. It is at the City’s discretion to place non-legal (display)
advertisements in any publication regardless of bid participation.

Staff respectfully requests the Liaisons review and provide feedback on the methodology to be
used for the FY 2025-26 Bid.
